85	  const [, maybeAlias, ...rest] = pathname.split('/');
86	  if (!maybeAlias || !getSiteUrlAliases().has(maybeAlias)) return pathname;
87	  return `/${rest.join('/')}`;

# PRD – Data Migration, SEO, GEO & URL

*Last updated: 2026-06-11*

Scope: Magento→SFCC data migration, URL strategy and redirects, SEO (canonicals/hreflang, sitemaps/robots, rendering/headings/meta, structured data), and GEO routing foundations. Regional storefront routing, consent, and currency live in [regional.md](regional.md).

---

## 1. Data Migration (DMU-001 – DMU-012)

- Product feed via MuleSoft from AP21 to SFCC covering ~1,600 active SKUs: names, descriptions, attributes, imagery refs, category assignments (DMU-001). Ongoing product sync via MuleSoft post-migration. **DMU-002 — Confirmed (status flipped from Ready for Sign Off, 2026-06-11).** The PWA-side contract is settled: SFCC displays exactly what MuleSoft returns for product data (JT 04-06), with AP21 as the master of record. Upstream sourcing (the first load draws from **both AP21 and PLM** via MuleSoft, with Magento-enriched data migrated after the initial load) sits **outside the PWA boundary** — the PWA does not enrich or compute product attributes itself, it renders the MuleSoft payload. The earlier RJ challenges (PLM/Magento enrichment) are upstream-of-MuleSoft concerns, not PWA blockers.
- Multi-region catalogue assignments and regional merchandising preserved across all storefronts (DMU-003).
- Registered customer records (DMU-004, updated 2026-05-25): **only email address and Omneo ID** are migrated to SFCC. Name, phone number, saved delivery addresses, and communication preferences are sourced **live from Omneo at login**, not held in SFCC. The previously requested 20-address cap is no longer relevant (addresses are not stored in SFCC). FE must treat Omneo as the source of customer profile data post-login; degrade gracefully if Omneo is unreachable.
- **Customer passwords are not migrated** — customers must reset on first login (DMU-005). See AGENTS.md "Magento password migration" gotcha.
- Saved payment card details are **not** migrated; customers re-enter at next purchase (DMU-006).
- Historical order records are **not** migrated into SFCC. Order history is accessed via NewStore **through MuleSoft** where customer identifiers match across online and in-store channels (DMU-007, **Confirmed 2026-06-11** — status flipped from Ready for Sign Off). The PWA displays exactly what MuleSoft returns for customer order history (JT 04-06); no order data is held in SFCC. ⚠️ Source-of-truth flag retained: the requirement text + JT name **NewStore via MuleSoft**, while an RJ comment says **"Order history will come from Omneo"** — the upstream source (NewStore vs Omneo behind MuleSoft) is out of the PWA boundary but remains unreconciled; see Open Items. For the ME storefront, only online orders appear in My Account order history; the orders API returns the most recent 50 orders held in NewStore, and until NewStore transitions in ME only online orders are visible — no FE customisation required to filter retail orders (DMU-008, Ready for Sign Off 2026-05-25).
- Contentful API connections reconfigured to point at the new platform; no bulk content re-entry needed (DMU-009, **challenged → Open** — RJ: no longer required as AS will be setting up Contentful; reconciliation pending). Mechanism note: Contentful integrates as the headless CMS via the **Salesforce App Exchange connector**, consuming content through the Contentful **delivery API** for all customer-facing pages across all storefronts (Third Party Integrations: CMS / Contentful) — i.e. the integration is the App Exchange connector, not a bespoke API rewire.
- Product images and digital assets (DMU-010, de-scoped 2026-05-25): **out of scope for migration.** Images and assets are stored and served from Contentful — there is no CDN migration, no asset URL rewrite, and no 301 redirects for asset URLs. The existing Contentful API connection is simply reconfigured to point at the new SFCC platform as part of go-live (covered by DMU-009). (Source note records the **new** platform CDN as **Akamai** (SFCC default), whereas the **current** setup is **Cloudflare** (DMU-020). These are not in conflict — they describe current vs new platform CDN — but the migration must carry existing Cloudflare redirect/SEO rules forward to Akamai; see §2 DMU-019/DMU-020. No asset-migration impact, as assets stay in Contentful.)
- Migration approach: initial bulk export + one or more timestamp-based delta migrations + a final delta close to DNS cutover (DMU-011). Migration scripts must be repeatable and capable of multiple delta runs — one-off scripts are not acceptable (DMU-012).
- **Wishlist migration (Confirmed):** customer wishlist data migrated from Magento, wishlist items mapped to corresponding SFCC product records and associated to the migrated account via Omneo ID. FE renders the migrated wishlist post-login.
- **Product enrichment migration (Confirmed):** badges, category assignments, colour swatches, colour grouping, swatch images, and Shop the Look associations migrated from Magento to SFCC, mapped to the corresponding product/catalogue structure (Shop the Look display logic TBD).
- **Notify Me migration (Confirmed):** active Notify Me (back-in-stock) subscriptions migrated from Magento — customer email addresses and product IDs carried forward and mapped to SFCC product records.

---

## 2. URL Strategy (DMU-013 – DMU-020)

- Existing storefront locale prefix conventions preserved (DMU-013) — see [regional.md](regional.md) Section 1.
- AU configured as root with no locale prefix and designated x-default hreflang target (DMU-016, **Resolved** — AU root stays globally crawlable; the bot allowlist in REG-009 exempts search engines and social unfurlers from the human geo-redirect, so `x-default` continues to point at the AU root).
- Existing product URL `.html` suffix preserved to maintain indexed URLs and avoid unnecessary 301 overhead (DMU-015).
- Category URLs updated for SEO consolidation (e.g. `/clothing/dresses`); 301s applied from all legacy category paths (DMU-014).
- 301 permanent redirects implemented for all URLs that change as a result of migration — products, categories, content, assets (DMU-017).
- All redirects implemented per the redirect mapping document, produced during build phase and validated pre go-live (DMU-018, **Open** — Accenture to propose redirect ownership; Zimmermann IT to review existing CDN rules).
- All 301s managed at CDN/edge level to minimise application-layer impact (DMU-019, **Open** — existing CDN redirect and SEO rules must be identified and carried forward, not auto-transferred).
- Existing CDN redirect rules and SEO configuration from the current Cloudflare setup preserved and carried forward to the new platform CDN (DMU-020).

---

## 3. SEO (DMU-021 – DMU-041)

### Canonicals & hreflang
- Canonical tags output on all indexable pages, referencing the preferred URL for the storefront (DMU-021).
- Filtered and faceted PLP URLs canonicalise to the unfiltered base PLP URL to prevent duplicate-content indexation (DMU-022, **Open** — Zimmermann wants the ability to override the canonical on selected indexable filter pages).
- hreflang tags applied only on canonical PDP URLs; non-canonical PDP variants do not carry hreflang but **do** retain canonical tags (DMU-023).
- hreflang implemented via XML sitemap format, mapping all locale codes to their respective storefront URLs (DMU-024).
- hreflang tags consolidated from the current 200+ country-specific tags to ~12 regional/language-level tags (DMU-025) — final structure to be confirmed with the Sparro SEO team prior to implementation.

### Sitemaps & robots
- XML sitemaps auto-generated per storefront and locale, refreshed daily (DMU-026). Disabled and deleted pages excluded on regeneration (DMU-027). Homepage URLs include trailing slash (DMU-028). URLs blocked in `robots.txt` must not appear in any sitemap (DMU-029).
- `robots.txt` permits crawling of indexable pages including the bag page; restricts checkout flow, account pages, search results, and filtered URL parameters (DMU-036).

### Rendering, headings & meta
- All product, category, and content pages rendered **server-side (SSR)** for full crawlability by search engines and AI bots without dependence on client-side JS (DMU-030).
- Title tags per page in the format `[Product Name] [Colour] | Zimmermann` — the legacy "Online" token has been removed as it consumes character space without value. Configurable via BM meta tag rules (DMU-031, updated 2026-05-15).
- Unique meta description tags per product and category page, sourced from product and catalogue data in SFCC. Category page metadata remains editable per page and is not auto-applied across all pages (DMU-032, Ready for Sign Off — Zimmermann to clarify what "auto-applied across pages" means before final sign-off).
- Single H1 per page template (homepage, PLP, PDP), correct H2–H6 hierarchy, no duplicate heading tags (DMU-033). PDP H1 includes the product colour (DMU-034).
- CMS-editable on-page SEO content field on all category and PLP pages, configurable at individual storefront level (DMU-035, partial resolution 2026-05-15): **SEO rules and attributes will live in SFCC per storefront** (not Contentful). Still Open: Sparro to define field schema before custom build.

### Structured data
- Product and Merchant Listing Schema on all PDPs per Sparro template (DMU-037) — custom build required, not OOTB in SFCC PWA Kit.
- CollectionPage, BreadcrumbList, and ItemList Schema on all PLPs per Sparro template (DMU-038) — custom build, Accenture + Sparro to confirm JSON-LD scope and page types.
- LocalBusiness Schema on individual boutique location detail pages per Sparro template (DMU-039) — custom build.
- Organisation Schema on each regional storefront homepage per Sparro template, with `url` and `contactPoint` fields configured per storefront (DMU-040) — custom build.
- Structured data for products includes available sizes and per-offer availability, driven by real-time inventory data (DMU-041).

---

## 4. GEO (DMU-042)

The system will deliver the technical foundations required for **post-launch GEO (Generative Engine Optimisation) enablement** — SSR, structured data, canonical URLs, and XML sitemaps — ensuring no architectural decisions block future GEO activation (DMU-042). No GEO-specific features are in launch scope.

---

## 5. Open Items

See **AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies"** for the full list. Data migration / URL / SEO / GEO open items:

- Redirect mapping ownership and existing CDN/SEO rule audit (DMU-018, DMU-019)
- PLP canonical override on indexable filter pages (DMU-022)
- Category meta description "auto-applied across pages" — Zimmermann to clarify the concern before sign-off (DMU-032)

I have everything. Here is the evidence-led picture.

---

# SEO Infrastructure Audit — zimmermann-pwa

Versions: `@salesforce/retail-react-app@10.0.0`, `@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk@3.18.0`, `@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime@3.18.0`, `react-helmet@6.1.0`, `helmet@4.6.0`.

## 1. The `Seo` component

**No override exists.** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/seo/` does not exist (confirmed via `ls` — "No such file or directory"). Every consumer imports the base package path.

Base: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/seo/index.jsx` — 35 lines total. Props: `title`, `description`, `noIndex` (bool), `keywords`, `children`, plus `...props` spread onto `<Helmet>`. It renders (lines 16–24) a `<Helmet>` containing `<title>{title ? \`${title} | ${DEFAULT_SITE_TITLE}\` : DEFAULT_SITE_TITLE}</title>`, and conditionally `<meta name="description">`, `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` (noindex only, never nofollow), `<meta name="keywords">`, then `{children}`.

**Live defect worth costing:** `DEFAULT_SITE_TITLE` is `'Retail React App'` (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants.js:13`) and is **not overridden anywhere** — `grep "SITE_TITLE"` across `overrides/app/constants/` returns nothing. So every `<Seo title=...>` page renders `"… | Retail React App"`, and `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx:413` emits `<meta name="apple-mobile-web-app-title" content="Retail React App" />`.

Consumers in `overrides/`:
| File | Usage |
|---|---|
| `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx:411` | `<Seo>` with children (no title/description) — sitewide |
| `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx:55-59` | `title="Home Page"`, `description="Commerce Cloud Retail React App"`, `keywords="Commerce Cloud, Retail React App, React Storefront"` — **placeholder boilerplate still shipping** |
| `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx:347-349` | `title`/`description` + child `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow" />` |
| `overrides/app/pages/categoryPath/index.tsx:74` | `<Seo noIndex />` (not-found branch only) |
| `overrides/app/pages/contentfulPreview/index.tsx:149,161,172` | `<Seo noIndex />` |
| `overrides/app/components/contentful/experienceBySlug/index.tsx:64,78,148,164` | `<Seo noIndex />` (error/preview branches only) |

Base-package consumers: `_app/index.jsx:91`, `pages/home`, `pages/registration`, `pages/reset-password`, `pages/account`, `pages/login`.

**Gap:** `categoryPath` (`/:segments+` catch-all — the real PLP/content route per `overrides/app/routes.tsx:109-110`) and `experienceBySlug` only mount `<Seo>` on their *failure* branches. The success branch of the catch-all emits **no title and no description at all** — it falls through to `_app`'s bare `<Seo>`, i.e. literally `<title>Retail React App</title>`.

## 2. Helmet usage in `overrides/`

Five call sites. `react-helmet` has no types — a local shim exists at `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts:150-167`.

**`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1109-1118`**
```jsx
<Helmet>
  <title>{product?.pageTitle}</title>
  {product?.pageMetaTags?.length > 0 &&
    product.pageMetaTags.map(({ id, value }) => (
      <meta name={id} content={value} key={id} />
    ))}
  {/* Fallback for description if not included in pageMetaTags */}
  {!product?.pageMetaTags?.some((tag) => tag.id === 'description') &&
    product?.pageDescription && <meta name="description" content={product.pageDescription} />}
</Helmet>
```

**`overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:1250-1257`**
```jsx
<Helmet>
  <title>{category?.pageTitle ?? searchQuery}</title>
  <meta name="description" content={category?.pageDescription ?? searchQuery ?? undefined} />
  <meta name="keywords" content={category?.pageKeywords} />
  {productSearchResult?.pageMetaTags?.map(({ id, value }) => {
    return <meta name={id} content={value} key={id} />;
  })}
</Helmet>
```

**`overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx:183-185`** — `<Helmet htmlAttributes={{ lang: locale }}>` containing only `<link rel="preconnect" href={CONTENTFUL_IMAGE_CDN_ORIGIN} />`. And `:231-235` — conditional `<Helmet><meta name={CSP_NONCE_META_NAME} content={cspNonce} /></Helmet>`.

**`overrides/app/pages/checkout/partials/payment.tsx:167-169`** — Adyen stylesheet link only, no SEO relevance.

### What meta is emitted today
| Tag | Status |
|---|---|
| `<title>` | Yes — PDP `product.pageTitle`, PLP `category.pageTitle ?? searchQuery`, else `"Retail React App"` |
| `description` | Yes — PDP (pageMetaTags or fallback), PLP (`category.pageDescription`) |
| `keywords` | PLP only |
| `robots` | Only `noindex` on preview/404 branches + `noindex, nofollow` on recentlyViewed. **Nothing sets `index, follow`** — PDP/PLP pass through whatever SFCC `pageMetaTags` happens to contain |
| `canonical` | **None. Zero `rel="canonical"` anywhere in `overrides/`, `config/`, `worker/`, or `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`** |

## 6. CSP — and the real answer on JSON-LD

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts`, 275 lines. `useDefaults: true` (`:116`). `script-src` is at `:131-151` — an allowlist of third-party hosts only (Google Maps/Places, Adyen, Stripe, PayPal, Apple Pay, Measmerize, Klarna, `storage.googleapis.com`, `*.demandware.net`).

Two things matter here:

**(a) There is no `'unsafe-inline'` and no nonce in `script-src`.** The nonce machinery in this file (`getOrCreateNonce`, `:96-112`) is **`style-src-elem` only** — built for SFCC-856 / Chakra-emotion and Contentful's un-nonceable injected `<style>` tags. `:183` is the only nonce consumer. `script-src` never receives a nonce or a hash.

Note also the two-layer merge: `overrides/app/ssr.js:129` applies `defaultPwaKitSecurityHeaders` **before** `helmet()` at `:131-135`. The runtime middleware patches `res.setHeader` and unions its required directives into whatever helmet emits (`node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime/utils/middleware/security.js:40` — `'script-src': ["'self'", "'unsafe-eval'", runtimeAdmin, siteDotCom]`; union at `:107`). Final effective `script-src` ≈ the app allowlist ∪ `'self' 'unsafe-eval'` + MRT admin + site.com. Still no `'unsafe-inline'`, still no nonce.

**(b) This does not block JSON-LD.** `<script type="application/ld+json">` is a *data block*, not an executable script — the HTML spec's "prepare the script element" algorithm never classifies it as classic/module, so it is never executed and the CSP inline-script check is never invoked. Emitting JSON-LD requires **no CSP change**. I want to be precise rather than reassuring here, so three caveats for the estimate:

1. **Do not attach a nonce to the JSON-LD tag "to be safe."** Under CSP3, introducing any nonce or hash into `script-src` disables `'unsafe-inline'` for the whole directive. This file already documents that exact footgun biting them twice in `style-src-elem` (`:37-41` and `:200-209`, the latter noting a live 2026-09-07 breakage). Adding a nonce to `script-src` risks the same class of regression against `'unsafe-eval'`/third-party payment scripts.
2. **React-helmet + JSON-LD content must go through `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`** or a single string child. Passing an object or interpolated fragments to a `<script>` child under helmet is a known source of silent empty output — budget a little time to verify the SSR'd bytes, not just the React tree.
3. **`script-src-attr` is `'none'`** (helmet default, not overridden) — irrelevant to JSON-LD, but means no inline event handlers if any vendor snippet is ever inlined.

Other relevant CSP state: `'frame-ancestors': ["'self'", 'https://app.contentful.com']` (`:273`), `'style-src-attr': ["'unsafe-inline'"]` (`:218`), and `STRICT_CSP_PATH_PREFIXES` (`:48-61`) route-gating with site-alias stripping (`:84-88`) — note that list must stay in sync with `overrides/app/routes.tsx` if new SEO routes (e.g. a sitemap route) are added.

## Bottom line for estimating

**Exists today:** SSR on all routes (Helmet SSR-injected, `script` whitelisted); base `Seo` component (title/description/noindex/keywords, un-overridden); PDP/PLP title+description from SFCC `pageMetaTags`; a permissive static `robots.txt`; self-referential hreflang inherited verbatim from the base template; a well-documented CSP with per-request nonces on `style-src-elem` only.

**Does not exist at all:** canonical tags (any page), cross-site hreflang, XML sitemaps, OG/Twitter cards, structured data of any kind, per-storefront robots, and any `index, follow` affirmation. `DEFAULT_SITE_TITLE` is still `"Retail React App"`, the homepage still ships placeholder SEO copy, and the `/:segments+` catch-all — which serves the real PLP and content pages — emits no page-specific title or description on its success path.

**Three estimate-shaping gotchas:** (1) `supportedLocales.length === 1` per site means hreflang needs a brand-new cross-site resolver, not a tweak; (2) `og:` tags from Business Manager are currently rendered with `name=` instead of `property=` and are therefore inert; (3) JSON-LD needs no CSP change, but do not add a `script-src` nonce — this repo has already been burned twice by the CSP3 nonce-disables-unsafe-inline rule.
